presentation.pitch: Atomic Design organizes an interface into five levels: small elements, useful groups, complete sections, page layouts and finished screens.
focus: Explain what each of the five levels represents.
Use a button, a labeled field, a table and Overview as familiar examples.
Show how reusable pieces become a complete screen.

atom.title: Atoms · Button
atom.summary: A single interface element, such as a button, an input or a label. Each has one simple purpose.
talk: A single interface element, such as a button, an input or a label. Each has one simple purpose.

molecule.title: Molecules · Labeled field

organism.title: Organisms · Data table
organism.summary: A larger group of components that forms a useful section, such as a data table or navigation header.

flows.title: High-level diagram
flows.lead: Atomic Design organizes an interface into five levels: small elements, useful groups, complete sections, page layouts and finished screens.
flows.heading: From small pieces to a complete screen

lanes.title: The five levels of Atomic Design
lanes.caption: Each level combines smaller pieces into something more complete.

steps.title: The smallest building blocks
steps.text: A single interface element, such as a button, an input or a label. Each has one simple purpose.

steps.title: Small groups with one job
steps.text: A few atoms working together, such as an input with its label and help text.

steps.title: Complete sections of an interface
steps.text: A larger group of components that forms a useful section, such as a data table or navigation header.

steps.title: The layout of a page
steps.text: A reusable arrangement of sections. It defines where the heading, metrics, chart and table belong.

steps.title: The finished screen
steps.text: A template filled with content and data that people can use, such as the Overview screen showing observations.

boundaries: Use the same buttons, fields and sections across different screens.
Shared components make appearance and interaction feel familiar.
A template provides the arrangement. A page fills it with content and data.
